markdown_report:
**Evidence and directions.** Three starting-point insights guide the experiment. First, all four perturbation panels completed zero users because routing was unavailable. Explicit routes and coverage checks are prerequisites for interpreting sensitivity. Second, Electronics has a 13.59% sampled training-pair inversion rate. This motivates investigation but identifies neither recency failure nor validation accuracy. Third, deletion changes content and positions. Fixed-slot replacements and multiset-preserving swaps provide complementary controls, although neither establishes realistic counterfactual behavior.

Three literature insights strengthen the design. Activation-patching conclusions depend on corruption and measurement choices [1]. Positional-attention research motivates separating position from item semantics [2]; SASRec and AC-TSR additionally support simple position ablations [4,5]. Sampled metrics can disagree with catalog rankings [3], so diagnostics, pinned selection and catalog recommendations require separate interpretation.

**Framework.** Cross intervention locus (identity, order, positional contribution), evidence level (fitted-target sensitivity, training comparison, host validation), and coverage (user, category, four-category macro). Add perturbation energy as a control dimension. The gap is a completed comparison connecting a specified regularizer to host outcomes; diagnostic treatment selection remains a separate hypothesis [6].

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more implementation work.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routed fixed-slot recency audit | 3/6/3 | Inexpensive reproducible controls | Measurement alone offers no training improvement |
| Positional dropout with item and energy controls [1,2,4] | 4/6/5 | Small intervention with stronger component comparison | Established regularization; energy matching remains incomplete |
| Candidate-distribution stress audit [3] | 3/6/5 | Exposes dependence on easy candidates | Catalog scoring costs compute; targets remain fitted |
| Remove positional embeddings [4,5] | 2/6/3 | Simple architectural control | Removes useful order information and tests another mechanism |

**Selected idea: controlled positional regularization.** At 10% progress, retain baseline, positional-dropout and item-dropout arms with additional probability 0.1. Preserve existing embedding dropout. Equal probabilities inject unequal expected noise energy: E‖δx‖²=p‖x‖²/(1−p). Add an energy-matched item control, freezing its probability from a seeded initialization calibration; report realized energy during training. This strengthens comparison without proving component-specific importance.

Repair routing and complete the frozen baseline diagnostic panel: fitted training targets, identical candidates, unchanged-input checks, fixed-slot replacements retaining the final conditioning item, and earlier-position swaps. Missing coverage remains unavailable. Across-arm diagnostics are descriptive; no diagnostic deployment rule is justified.

Train with synchronized shared randomness and a dedicated experimental-mask stream. Select complete arms solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; retain all category outcomes. Preserve seeds, splits, epochs, predictor generation and interfaces. Original arms require twelve category fits; the added control requires four more. Fit only within declared remaining compute ceilings. One seed and repeated validation selection limit robustness and invite selection overfitting [7]; no improvement is established.

References: [1] arXiv:2309.16042; [2] arXiv:2407.02793; [3] Krichene–Rendle, *On Sampled Metrics*; [4] arXiv:1808.09781; [5] AC-TSR, CIKM 2023; [6] Freidlin et al., PMC2911042; [7] Cawley–Talbot, JMLR 2010.

idea.description: Test positional-contribution dropout against unchanged SASRec, equal-probability item-contribution dropout, and an additional energy-matched item control when the complete comparison fits the remaining budget. Repair explicit diagnostic routing, characterize trained arms with frozen position-preserving fitted-target probes, and select solely using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
idea.motivation: No supplied perturbation panel completed any users, so the results cannot support a diagnostic deployment rule. Electronics has weaker sampled training separation, but neither those margins nor qualitative feedback identifies positional overreliance. The original equal-probability control also confounds component choice with perturbation energy. A bounded regularization pilot with explicit noise controls is feasible early research, while its novelty and diagnostic predictive value remain unestablished.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, original splits, and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Honor SASREC_EPOCHS with the matched default of 200. Do not inspect hidden test files, fetch additional datasets or pretrained weights, or change the host evaluator. No execution or measured improvement is claimed here.

Retain the original three arms: unchanged baseline, additional positional dropout p=0.1, and additional item dropout p=0.1. Keep the same existing embedding dropout in all arms. Identify the actual item and positional contributions immediately before addition, including the baseline's item-embedding scaling. Apply inverted elementwise dropout only to the assigned contribution during training. Preserve the baseline operation order, causal attention, padding treatment, objective, sampler, optimizer and checkpoint schedule. Additional dropout becomes identity during evaluation. Record the insertion point and probabilities in checkpoints. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the trained module, retain all routes, and verify evaluation logits match the training module on identical inputs. Training code was not supplied, so insertion details require verification against the actual baseline rather than assuming its internals.

Add a fourth, explicitly designated energy-matched item arm if its complete four-category fit fits the declared budget. Before observing intervention outcomes, initialize the baseline architecture with seed 42 independently for each category. Using a dedicated seed-0 training-data calibration stream, select up to 256 training users from sorted eligible IDs and construct their ordinary sampler-compatible sequences. Record exact IDs and sequences. Measure the mean squared norm per occupied position of the scaled item contribution S_item and positional contribution S_pos before existing dropout. Freeze E=(0.1/0.9)*S_pos and p_item_matched=E/(S_item+E). This matches expected total squared perturbation at initialization, not throughout optimization. If norms or probabilities are invalid, mark the arm unavailable; do not silently clamp or substitute a control. Report calibration counts and component norms. At a fixed once-per-epoch logging schedule, record predicted and realized perturbation energies on occupied positions using the masks already generated for training, without extra stochastic forward passes. Norm evolution, covariance, downstream sensitivity and normalization remain possible explanations even when energy matches. Equal-probability item dropout remains the originally proposed control and must be labeled energy-unmatched.

Use dedicated experimental mask generators keyed reproducibly by category and training step. Corresponding item and positional masks use aligned uniform draws across arms where shapes match. Experimental calls must not advance the baseline's initialization, ordering, negative-sampling or existing-dropout streams. Preserve the baseline random procedure rather than silently redesigning its sampler. Match initial weights, batches and negative samples across arms; log reproducible initialization and sampled-batch checksums. Where shared randomness cannot be synchronized reliably, disclose that limitation and weaken paired-training claims. Independent streams separate randomness sources; synchronized events align corresponding draws across arms. The required training seed remains 42: additional seed pairs are a future robustness study, not part of this matched task.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Attach dataset_name explicitly to each category view or supply diagnostic_views keyed by Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Never infer a route from local item IDs. Category-local calls are valid; aggregate only matching complete results from all four categories. Missing routes return actionable unavailable status. view.model must be the actual trained nn.Module; retain item_emb, log2feats and predict_score compatibility. Loader batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Preserve every module's training flag and Python, NumPy, CPU Torch and CUDA RNG states in a finally block. Use evaluation mode, no_grad and isolated generators. Preserve sampler or loader-generator state where exposed; otherwise use a dedicated diagnostic loader and report any remaining state limitation.

Freeze the bounded diagnostic panel from the verified unchanged baseline before inspecting intervention outcomes. For each category, use a local seed-0 permutation of sorted training user IDs to select up to 32 eligible users. Hold out the final public training interaction only within the diagnostic input; do not alter training or benchmark splits. Require a retained conditioning prefix of at least five items, right-aligned within model maximum length. The target may already have been fitted and is not an independent generalization target. Draw 99 unique negatives excluding padding and all of that user's training interactions; insufficient candidates make the user ineligible. Preserve the final conditioning item. Recent and older editable positions are the penultimate and earliest occupied slots. Match replacement presence elsewhere in the prefix and minimize squared differences in standardized log1p training frequency and baseline embedding norm, excluding original item and target. Standardize over nonpadding items, with standard deviations floored at 1e-8. Select five distinct replacements uniformly from the closest 50 eligible items, or all when fewer exist, using item-ID tie breaking and category-specific local streams. Record shortages and matching residuals. Freeze users, sequences, slots, candidates, replacements and baseline matching statistics across arms. Preserve padding, occupied positions, sequence length and timestamp slots. Include a recent/older swap preserving the item multiset and final item. These interventions do not independently identify absolute-position effects, preserve exact repetition multiplicity, or guarantee realistic transitions.

Score unchanged inputs twice. Rank candidates by descending score with ascending item-ID ties; diagnostic tie rules do not replace host semantics. Report repeated-score discrepancies, target-rank changes, hit@10 changes, top-ten overlap, final-feature cosine, coverage and eligibility. Define D as the user mean of recent-minus-older replacement rank change divided by 99, averaging replacement draws within user first. Report category effects and only complete four-category equal-weight summaries; missing or truncated panels produce null macro values. Any bootstrap intervals use 10,000 seed-0 paired user resamples within category, conditional on fitted models and frozen panels. They exclude seed variability and adaptive selection. Missing coverage prevents claims about diagnostic differences but does not itself prohibit an independently budgeted training comparison. Retain sampled training-margin and embedding-alignment diagnostics with counts and scope; average cosine is not proof of collapse or recommendation diversity. Include measured metrics, definitions, controls, missingness and limitations in the interpreter prompt.

The original three arms require twelve category fits if no exactly equivalent baseline can be reused; the fourth requires four additional fits. Freeze arm order as baseline, positional p=0.1, item p=0.1, then energy-matched item, along with checkpoint schedules and per-arm compute ceilings before new outcomes. Reuse a baseline only when initialization, code, data, schedule and artifacts match. Require externally tracked remaining method-wide budget before launch; no remaining balance is supplied here. Count training, diagnostics, debugging and failures against 43,200 GPU-seconds, with single-GPU execution per trial and aggregate accounting across concurrent host slots. Launch an arm only when its declared four-category ceiling fits. Record unfinished arms, failures and category scores without substituting partial-category macro values. Do not claim energy-controlled conclusions if the fourth arm is unavailable.

Select the highest supplied pinned macro validation HR@10 among complete arms, using a frozen tie priority favoring baseline, then positional, equal-probability item, and energy-matched item. Preserve host validation users, seed 42, 99 unique negatives and all evaluator semantics. Report every category result, equal-weight macro, validation query and comparison against baseline. When paired host hit indicators are actually exposed, use 10,000 seed-0 within-category paired user bootstrap resamples and report conditional difference intervals and discordant counts. Otherwise report aggregates only; never reconstruct hidden labels. One changed hit moves category HR@10 by 0.005 and macro HR@10 by 0.00125. Repeated checkpoint and intervention selection can overfit validation; intervals do not correct that bias.

This is an intervention pilot, not a test that diagnostics select treatments. Across-arm diagnostic changes are descriptive. A later diagnostic policy experiment would need frozen marker definitions, threshold, intervention mapping, fallback and comparisons against both always-baseline and always-intervention before observing its outcomes. Existing evidence remains exploratory. Four categories do not support strong dataset-level inference; under valid independent-category sign exchangeability, four nonzero paired differences give a minimum conventional one-sided exact sign-flip p-value of 1/16 and usual two-sided minimum of 2/16. Users, checkpoints and seeds do not add independent categories. Emphasize effect sizes, consistency and failures. The host's untouched final evaluation is external confirmation of the selected procedure; its unavailable outcomes must not be anticipated as evidence validating a diagnostic policy.

Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category using the selected model. Use public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps only. Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores and simulator diversity/conformity traits are unavailable despite the generic example schema. Treat ownership, compatibility, unwanted redundancy, intent and preference judgments as unknown unless supported by permitted evidence or explicit feedback. Semantic similarity and recurrence are observable proxies, not verified utility. Simple position removal, additional joint dropout and independently tuned item/position dropout remain declared follow-up controls; do not claim this pilot establishes superiority over those untested alternatives.
idea.pseudocode:
freeze original arms = [baseline, position_p0.1, item_p0.1]
freeze optional fourth arm = energy_matched_item
freeze arm order, tie priority, checkpoints, seeds and compute ceilings

for category in required_four_categories:
    initialize baseline architecture using unchanged seed-42 procedure
    freeze up to 256 seed-0 calibration training sequences
    S_item = mean squared scaled-item norm over occupied slots
    S_pos = mean squared positional norm over occupied slots
    E = (0.1 / 0.9) * S_pos
    p_matched[category] = E / (S_item + E)
    if calibration invalid:
        mark matched arm unavailable for category
    save initialization and calibration manifests

# Preserve baseline operation order and padding behavior.
item_part = baseline_scaled_item_contribution(sequence)
pos_part = baseline_position_contribution(sequence)
if training and arm != baseline:
    U = dedicated_uniforms(category, training_step, contribution_shape)
    if arm == position_p0.1:
        pos_part = pos_part * (U >= 0.1) / 0.9
    elif arm == item_p0.1:
        item_part = item_part * (U >= 0.1) / 0.9
    elif arm == energy_matched_item:
        p = p_matched[category]
        item_part = item_part * (U >= p) / (1 - p)
x = baseline_embedding_dropout(item_part + pos_part)
x = baseline_padding_handling(x, sequence)

for arm in frozen_order:
    require declared complete-arm ceiling <= remaining_shared_budget
    otherwise record incomplete comparison and stop launching fits
    for category in required_four_categories:
        restore matched initialization and shared random-input procedure
        train with unchanged objective, sampler and schedule
        log initialization/batch checksums and scheduled noise energies
        set view.dataset_name = category
        keep view.model as actual trained module
        if arm == baseline:
            freeze category diagnostic users, candidates and replacements
        diagnose against frozen baseline panel where available
        ingest pinned host outcomes only when actually supplied
        record all compute, failures, missingness and validation queries

class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        preserve module flags and all accessible RNG/loader states
        try:
            resolve explicit category route or return unavailable status
            under eval mode and no_grad:
                measure supported margins and embedding alignment
                score unchanged histories twice
                score frozen fixed-slot replacements and swaps
                report definitions, paired effects, coverage and limitations
            return {metrics, metric_definitions}
        finally:
            restore preserved flags and states

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return prompt containing measured metrics, definitions, coverage,
           controls, fitted-target limitations and unobserved attributes

aggregate diagnostics only over complete matching four-category panels
report all complete-arm category and macro host validation scores
select complete arm by pinned macro HR@10 with frozen tie priority
if paired host hits are exposed:
    report discordant counts and stratified paired bootstrap differences
label diagnostic changes descriptive and validation selection exploratory
export selected four checkpoints through synchronized predictor writer
verify eval-logit agreement and all routes
produce twenty full-catalog unseen-item recommendation lists

originality.positive: The routed diagnostic panel and energy-controlled component comparison form a useful, falsifiable integration; independent positional dropout is not established by the supplied precedents.
originality.negative: Dropout, noise-energy matching, positional ablations and paired perturbation controls are established techniques. Lack of an exact supplied precedent does not establish novelty.

future_potential.positive: A completed pilot could clarify whether positional regularization merits further study and provide reusable infrastructure for prospective diagnostic treatment-selection experiments.
future_potential.negative: Four categories, fitted diagnostic targets, one prescribed training seed and adaptive validation reuse limit generalization. Equal energy still leaves covariance and downstream sensitivity confounded.

code_difficulty.positive: The architecture change remains small and preserves deterministic SASRec inference; energy calibration needs only training inputs and embedding contributions.
code_difficulty.negative: Event-synchronized randomness, state-safe diagnostics, frozen cross-model manifests, predictor checks and up to sixteen category fits make the complete study moderately demanding.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Shows that corruption and measurement choices affect activation-patching conclusions.
Motivates explicit intervention definitions, unchanged-input checks and cautious interpretation.
limitations: Studies language models rather than this SASRec benchmark.
Does not establish positional-dropout effectiveness or make the proposed replacement histories realistic.

related_work.title: Learning Positional Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Investigates positional information in sequential recommendation.
Motivates separating positional relations from item semantics.
limitations: Does not establish positional overreliance in the supplied checkpoints.
Does not validate the dropout probability, energy-matching rule or diagnostic policy.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking comparisons can disagree with full-catalog comparisons.
Supports separating sampled diagnostics, pinned benchmark selection and catalog recommendation behavior.
limitations: Does not identify the cause of Electronics training-pair errors.
Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Introduces SASRec and applies dropout after combining item and positional embeddings.
Reports dataset-dependent effects of positional embeddings and benefits from ordinary dropout in its evaluated settings.
limitations: Does not isolate independent item-versus-position dropout.
Published ablations do not predict gains on the four matched RecHarness categories.

related_work.title: Attention Calibration for Transformer-based Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Separates order and distance calibration from item-driven attention.
Provides nearby evidence motivating simple positional ablations.
limitations: Its architecture and datasets differ from this experiment.
Does not establish superiority of independently applied positional dropout.

related_work.title: Stochastic Shared Embeddings: Data-driven Regularization of Embedding Layers
contributions: Provides the stochastic shared embedding approach used in SSE-PT.
Studies separately controlled stochastic replacement of embedding identities, offering a nearby regularization precedent.
limitations: Stochastic embedding replacement differs from elementwise contribution dropout.
The personalized sequential architecture and published scores do not establish RecHarness improvements.

related_work.title: PyTorch Dropout documentation
contributions: Documents Bernoulli masking and inverse-retention scaling during training.
Supports deriving expected squared perturbation energy p/(1-p) times the squared input norm.
limitations: Documents an operation rather than evidence of recommendation effectiveness.
Matching total expected energy does not match covariance, normalization effects or downstream sensitivity.

related_work.title: Random Number Generation for Simulation
contributions: Discusses random-number streams and common-random-number comparisons.
Motivates separating randomness sources and synchronizing corresponding events across intervention arms.
limitations: Does not guarantee lower variance for every neural training comparison.
Dedicated generators alone do not ensure that batches, examples and stochastic events remain aligned.

related_work.title: Randomized Clinical Trials With Biomarkers: Design Issues
contributions: Distinguishes biomarker-dependent treatment effects from evaluation of treatment-selection strategies.
Motivates freezing diagnostic policies and comparing them with always-baseline and always-intervention strategies.
limitations: Clinical trial designs are an analogy rather than an established recommendation protocol.
The proposed regularization pilot has no frozen diagnostic treatment-selection policy and cannot establish diagnostic predictive value.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimizing a finite-sample model-selection criterion can overfit that criterion.
Supports separating exploratory validation selection from independent confirmation.
limitations: Does not quantify selection bias for this particular search.
Freezing a new comparison cannot make previously inspected evidence independent.

related_work.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks
contributions: Emphasizes benchmark variability and limits of conclusions from restricted experimental samples.
Supports reporting uncertainty, effect sizes and sources of variation.
limitations: Does not supply additional independent datasets for this task.
The stated four-category sign-flip probability bounds follow from enumeration under explicit assumptions, rather than constituting an empirical finding of this paper.
